name: Stardew
lede: Stardew is a moderate, slightly greyed blue from the Maerz and Paul dictionary of color.

sections.title: A blue from plate 35
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary places this hue on plate 35, swatch F7, first recorded in 1928, and the ISCC-NBS circular of 1955 cites the same entry, classing it a grayish blue, Munsell notation 4.5PB 4.8/6.0 [1]. The books read give no story for the name itself, and its origin is undocumented here [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[chapman-s-blue]], [[jay-blue]] and [[tyrian-blue]], at 2.7, 3.7 and 3.9 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Stardew covers at least one per cent of the canvas in 154 paintings, about 0.65 per cent overall, more common than 57 per cent of the named colors we track; the within-painting lens finds it in 87 [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 15 of 1,674 paintings, present in 0.9 per cent of the 1,674 paintings (15 of them) we hold from that century, 1.7 times the archive's overall rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 44 per cent of its 87 appearances [2].

The earliest dated painting to carry it is from 1405, by Spinello Aretino, the same painting that also marks the earliest archive appearance of [[shadow-blue]], 525 years before the name's own 1930 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. A single early panel surfacing as the first match for more than one of today's named blues says more about how few paintings this old survive in the archive than about any dye in use at the time [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
